newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco talks work out cigarette price rises - paper.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco talks work out cigarette price rises - paper.

text.p: The tobacco industry is working out a proposal in settlement talks which would have cigarette makers raise prices in tandem while they subsidized a payment which could be as high as $300 billion, the Wall Street Journal said on Tuesday.

According to people participating in the negotiations, there were anxieties in the industry that Philip Morris would gain special benefits from advertising curbs proposed in talks, the paper said in its electronic edition.

Negotiators have proposed banning the use of human and cartoon figures from cigarette ads, the paper said. While Philip Morris would bid farewell to its Marlboro man, it could still use scenery of the western United States to get the same message across, the Journal said.
Philip Morris's rivals seek provisions which would prevent the financially strong cigarette maker from keeping prices under those of weaker competitors, the newspaper said.
Under plans proposed in the negotiations, the industry would pay $8 billion to $10 billion a year, funding the cost with a retail price hike of $0.50 per pack on cigarettes.
"There's clear tension between Philip Morris and those who think Philip Morris is using the money issue to drive them out," the newspaper quoted one person participating in the talks as saying.
Philip Morris was not immediately available to comment.
